claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have an 8-year-old son named Alex who lives with you at home. That's a good start.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care - meaning you pay for things like his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I take care of all his daily needs - his food, clothes, school things, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living in any residential accommodation paid for by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was in care for a couple of months earlier, but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need to understand this situation better:

**How long ago did Alex return home from care, and does he spend at least 24 hours a week at home now that he's back with you full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's back home with me full-time now - he lives here completely. It's been a little while since he came back.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Just to clarify the timeline:

**Approximately how many weeks or months ago did Alex return home from care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see what you're asking. Actually, let me be clearer - the time he was in care was about 8 weeks total, and that's finished now. He's been back home living with me full-time since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex was in care for 8 weeks total, and he's now back home with you full-time.

I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status that gives you the right to live here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have the right to live here in the UK.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
✓ He lives with you in the UK
✓ You're responsible for his day-to-day care and expenses
✓ You have the right to reside in the UK
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
✓ Although Alex was in care for 8 weeks, he's now back home with you full-time

You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you had been receiving Child Benefit before Alex went into care and it was stopped, you may need to inform HMRC that he's returned home so your payments can resume.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
